recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Revisit only if the work group wants a new, broader non-terminology best-practice section for invalid base-FHIR data generally; that broader policy is outside the necessary reconciliation for this terminology-binding issue.
issue_request: FHIR-25183 was Published with resolution Not Persuasive with Modification for R5, asking for guidance on historical, patient-provided, third-party, international, and otherwise poorly coded data when required or extensible value set bindings make mapping difficult.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by git commit 20773ceb3e13dbd52890f695c523c2b7e6cddada, which added a "Bindings and legacy data" section to source/terminologies.html covering required/extensible binding consequences, Additional Binding/current, Resource.meta.profile, and _profile search.
additional_context: The Jira resolution named Best Practices for Implementers, but the related Jira URL/page was the core terminologies/extensible-binding page. Confluence minutes for 2022-05-16 record the FHIR-I motion and rationale that additional-binding can distinguish all-data from current-data binding scope without solving per-instance current/non-current signaling. The linked Zulip discussion rejects a broad non-conformance flag and supports using binding/profile mechanisms. Duplicate FHIR-25184 is the same request.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active Using Codes/Terminologies page still contains the material guidance requested by the issue, and later source history preserved it while updating the Additional Binding link to the in-build ElementDefinition.binding.additional definition.

related_jiras.note: Same summary and description as FHIR-25183, marked Duplicate, so it was treated as background rather than a separate reconciliation target.
